As expected, following the 11.0 melee re-work a bunch of the melee weapons needed additional tweaks and changes once we saw how they performed in the real world. In the case of the Dagger, one of the initial issues we saw were issues pertaining to getting onto targets and being able to hit them reliably, these changes aim to address that
Increased lunge distance on primary and secondary attacks from 4.5m to 5m
Increased the secondary attack's sweep time slightly, to help ensure that backstabs can more reliably hit targets at max lunge distance
Increased Precision zone angle from 8 to 9 degrees, making it slightly easier to land precise strikes
Increased lunge distance on primary attacks from 4.5m to 5m
Increased max lunge speed slightly to support the increased lunge distance
Increased player movement speed when using the Deflect stance by 25%

There is also a quality of life change here how the Cross Slash attack's lunge works to make it slightly more reliable

Prior to 11.0, and despite its high utility, the KS-23 lagged behind a lot of other Heavy weapons and we wanted to address that. There were worries that the weapon was being 'slept on', but we felt it was time for a change to try and help the weapon regardless. Sometimes, making a change is the only way to find 'the truth' of why it performs as it does across all the different modes, skill tiers and so on. We can see from the last few weeks on live that the increase to 110 damage was too much, so we're reducing it to 104 with this update to break some of the attack combo breakpoints and lower DPS. We do still think the pre-11.0 KS-23 needed a small buff, hence not returning to 100 damage per shot immediately, but we'll continue to monitor how it plays at 104 damage and will adjust it again in later updates if we feel it's needed

We've seen feedback from some players who feel the Riot Shield has lost a lot of its power with the 11.0 update and the changes here to the Precision angle, lunge distance and damage are to address that to some extent. That said, we want to state that the changes made to Riot Shield in 11.0 were very deliberately aimed at giving it a new style of play and role, one that more reliably allows tanking of damage as well as acting as an 'anchor' for team fights and objective defense. On Medium, we want Dual Blades to be the more aggressive push-forwards brawling melee weapon, while the Riot Shield is more defensive and about stalling opposing players or anchoring fights, and we think the Riot Shield is definitely able to fill that role more now than it could prior to 11.0. We'll continue to monitor how it performs as the season goes on and will adjust as we need to
